:::{#exm-cov-vec-x}
#### The variance-covariance matrix of two events on one die roll

Roll a fair six-sided die once.
Let $X_1 = 1$ if the roll is even and $X_1 = 0$ otherwise,
and let $X_2 = 1$ if the roll is at least 4 and $X_2 = 0$ otherwise.
Each of $X_1$ and $X_2$ is 1 on three of the six equally likely outcomes, so

$$
\ba
\E{X_1} &= \E{X_1^2} = \frac{3}{6} = \frac{1}{2},
\\
\E{X_2} &= \E{X_2^2} = \frac{1}{2},
\ea
$$

since $X_i^2 = X_i$ for a variable that takes only the values 0 and 1.
The product $X_1 X_2$ is 1 only when the roll is 4 or 6, so $\E{X_1 X_2} = 2/6 = 1/3$.
By @thm-alt-cov:

$$
\ba
\Covs{X_1}{X_1} &= \E{X_1^2} - \paren{\E{X_1}}^2 = \frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{4} = \frac{1}{4},
\\
\Covs{X_2}{X_2} &= \frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{4} = \frac{1}{4},
\\
\Covs{X_1}{X_2} &= \E{X_1 X_2} - \E{X_1}\E{X_2} = \frac{1}{3} - \frac{1}{4} = \frac{1}{12}.
\ea
$$

So by @def-cov-vec-x, $\vX = \tp{(X_1, X_2)}$ has variance-covariance matrix

$$
\Varf{\vX} = \pmat{1/4 & 1/12 \\ 1/12 & 1/4}.
$$

:::
